messages:
maria (support): FYI — Customer AcmePay opened ticket #2345. They say streaming chat responses drop tool-call frames when structured-output mode is on. Repro on prod region us-west-2. Attached logs and a short K/V of events.
kevin (product): thanks. how severe is customer impact? is this consistent or intermittent?
eva (sales): AcmePay uses streaming to power a live billing UI. Missing tool-call frames causes charge rendering to stall; customer is blocking on an SLA review. They marked it high.
maria (support): appears after our 2024-11-14 runtime deploy (deploybot reported rollout). They see ~10% of streams missing the "tool_call" event entirely. Intermittent but reproducible on long sessions (~>20 tokens).
aj (eng): hmm. sounds like event framing or a flush issue with structured streaming path. can you paste a minimal streamed payload they expect vs what they see?
maria (support): pasted minimal example from logs:
```
--stream-start--
{ "event": "message", "text": "Here's the invoice" }
{ "event": "tool_call", "name": "render_invoice", "args": {"id": 123} }
{ "event": "structured_output", "schema": {"invoice": {}} }
--stream-end--
```
kevin (product): ok, customer expects the tool_call between message and structured_output. if the tool_call disappears the UI never calls the renderer. we need acceptance criteria to scope a fix: P0 would be a rollback/fast patch; P1 is targeted fix + canary; P2 backlog. What does Eng recommend?
sahil (eng-runtime): can reproduce locally with induced chunking. seems like our streaming framing merges small events into a single write under specific batching/window sizes -> parser on client drops second inline object. probable root cause: missing boundary token when structured mode enabled (we switched encoders in the last deploy).
aj (eng): agree w/ sahil. two remediation options: 1) server-side: add explicit frame delimiters for structured events (quick but changes protocol), 2) runtime: change batching/window to always flush after tool_call events (safer).
kevin (product): product considerations: change protocol requires API announcement & migration plan. prefer runtime fix if latency/cost hit isn't large. need test plan and rollout criteria.
eva (sales): customer will accept a small rollout window. they want ETA and whether a temporary non-streaming fallback is possible for critical paths.
aj (eng): temp mitigation: support can toggle non-streaming for the customer's key route (per-route flag) — that avoids missing frames but increases tail latency. I can ship a per-route toggle this week (patch). Longer fix: runtime flush change, needs QA and perf testing.
maria (support): i'm ok toggling non-streaming for AcmePay. Please provide exact route name and steps to flip.
sahil (eng-runtime): plan: triage ticket -> patch per-route fallback (hotfix) -> runtime flush change in next minor with canary. Acceptance criteria for the runtime change: 1) 99.9% of test streams preserve event order & all event objects across load tests, 2) no >5% tail latency regression in 95th pct, 3) no increase in token cost >3% for typical workloads.
kevin (product): that's good. please create a tracking issue in the product backlog with: customer impact summary, repro snippet, proposed hotfix + long-term fix, testing criteria above, rollout plan, and estimated effort (hotfix: 1 engineer 2 days, runtime fix: 2 engineers 2-3 sprints). Tag release and support.
aj (eng): I'll file the issue and link the deploy PRs. assigning initial owner: aj for hotfix, sahil for runtime change.
ops-bot: deploy log: rollout v2024.11.14 completed at 2024-11-14T03:21:10Z (no errors).
kevin (product): priority: P1 (customer SLA impact but workable with per-route fallback). Maria, please confirm when you flip the route and if customer still sees failures.
maria (support): will do. flipping route after business hours today. I'll update this thread with timestamps and customer confirmation. :thumbsup:
